speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with a pruritic rash on your bilateral upper extremities; can you describe exactly when the rash started and if the itch is constant or intermittent?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel, Liver_Function_Tests, Renal_Function_Tests, ESR
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_Clinical_Photographs

speaker: Doctor
text: The initial blood work and metabolic panels are all within normal limits. Regarding the rash on your arms, have you noticed any new soaps, detergents, or clothing materials you've been using recently, or do you recall any bug bites or exposure to poison ivy?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is a very long duration for a rash; has the itching become worse at night or do you see any burrows or lines on your wrists and finger web spaces? Also, does anyone in your household have a similar rash or symptoms of scabies?

REQUEST TEST: Scabies_Skin_Scraping

speaker: Doctor
text:
You mentioned the rash has persisted for five months without resolution; besides the wrists, do you see any tiny, thread-like burrows on your finger webs or elbows, and does the itching intensify significantly at night?

Also, have you had close contact with anyone else in your household or social circle who has experienced similar skin issues or unexplained itching?

REQUEST TEST: Scabies_Skin_Scraping

speaker: Doctor
text:
The repeated normal scabies scrapings make infestation unlikely despite the intense nocturnal itching you described. Given the 5-month duration, bilateral distribution, and lack of infectious etiology, do you notice any swelling of your fingers or other joints, and is your skin feeling tight or thickened?

REQUEST TEST: ANA, RF, ESR, CRP
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_High_Resolution_Photographs

speaker: Doctor
text:
The repeated negative scabies tests and your normal inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) make an infectious or systemic inflammatory cause unlikely. Given the 5-month duration, bilateral distribution, and lack of resolution, do you have any joint pain, morning stiffness, or photosensitivity? Are you experiencing any fatigue or fevers?

REQUEST TEST: Rheumatoid_Factor, Anti_CCP, ANA, ESR, CRP
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_High_Resolution_Photographs

speaker: Doctor
text:
I have received your results; the repeat autoimmune and inflammatory markers are also normal, which makes systemic lupus or vasculitis unlikely. Given the chronic 5-month duration, bilateral distribution, and negative workup for infection and systemic disease, do you notice any scaling, lichenoid bumps, or a pattern of small red dots (follicular papules) on your forearms? Are there any personal or family histories of psoriasis or autoimmune blistering diseases?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Pruritic Papular Eruption (likely secondary to an undiagnosed systemic condition or a chronic eczematous process, pending dermatologic biopsy)
